hooksDemo.description: Each card gets one field of paymentStore as a prop and calls useForm(field): it re-renders only when that field changes. Edit the fields on the Payment Form tab and come back.

storeContext.title: useStoreContext Demo
storeContext.subtitle: Non-reactive context (accountId, tenant) available in resolver/onSubmit via store.context
storeContext.description: useStoreContext sets a non-reactive bag of global variables — not form fields. Available in all callbacks via store.context.
storeContext.resolverNote: The users resolver reads store.context.accountId, so switching the account re-runs it by itself — watch the Users list reload. No resolver reads tenant: switching it requests nothing.

ssr.title: Server rendering
ssr.subtitle: A Server Component reads the rows and passes them as props. The client view creates its store with usePalistor, on the server and again in the browser, so the first HTML already has the data and the translations.

engineers.title: A list with data from the server
engineers.hint: The rows are passed as initialData: they are in the HTML, and the resolver is not called after hydration. Typing in the search sends one request, 300 ms after the last keystroke.
engineers.searchPlaceholder: A name or a focus, for example: compilers

projects.title: A list without server data
projects.hint: No initialData here. The server requests nothing and list.loading is already true there, so the HTML has the skeleton; the browser loads the rows.

summary.title: A Suspense group without server data
summary.hint: The group has resolve.options.suspense: true. The server sends the fallback of the Suspense boundary; the browser renders the content when the resolver returns.

form.subtitle: An editable form whose values come from the server. The resolvers' results arrive as initialData, so the HTML is complete and nothing is requested after hydration until a declared dependency changes.

profile.title: A profile prefilled by the server
profile.hint: The Server Component reads the profile and passes it as initialData. The group starts in the state its resolver's result would leave: the values are in the HTML, dirty and loading are false, and the resolver is not called after hydration. Edit a field and the group is dirty; reset() returns to the server's values, which stay the dirty baseline until a resolver run replaces them.
profile.name: Full name

deps.title: Declared dependencies
deps.hint: userId lives outside the profile group and is listed in resolve.deps of the profile and of the activity list. Choose another user: each resolver runs once. reload() runs the list's resolver again (a group has no reload()). A resolve that started from initialData has not run yet, so only its declared deps and contextDeps restart it: what its resolver merely reads is tracked from its first real run on.

errors.title: Errors reach the provider's notifier
errors.hint: Check a box, then reload the activity or choose another user. The request fails, the resolver's onError builds the message with ctx.t — the store's translator, so the toast is in the page's language — and calls ctx.notify, the notifier of PalistorProvider, which the store got in its constructor: a toast appears. A failed run changes no value: the profile keeps its values, the list keeps its rows and reports resolveStatus error with its error until a run succeeds.

draft.title: A draft over the server's data
draft.hint: A separate store with usePersist over localStorage. The server's HTML and the hydrating render show the server's announcement; after mount usePersist lays the saved draft over it, and the group is dirty against the server's data. Edit, reload the page: the draft comes back, and it starts no resolver. Discard: reset() returns to the server's values, persist.clear() removes the draft.

catalog.subtitle: Lists beyond the plain one: the first page of a paginated list, the first page of a load-more feed and the lists nested in rows come from the server as initialData. They are in the HTML, and hydration requests none of them again.

papers.title: Pages, the first one from the server
papers.hint: The server passes page 1 as initialData, the way the resolver returns it (items and total): the rows, the page count and the total are in the HTML, and hydration sends no request. Another page is one request; a page the list has already seen, page 1 included, comes from the cache without one.

milestones.title: Load more, the first page from the server
milestones.hint: pagination.mode: "infinite". The server's first page carries nextCursor: “Load more” sends one request with that cursor and appends one page. The last page answers nextCursor: null, and the feed ends, although that page is full.
milestones.shown: Showing {count} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} loaded

talks.title: Pages without server data
talks.hint: No initialData. The server requests nothing, but isInitialLoading is already true there, so the HTML has the skeleton; the browser loads page 1 once.

teams.title: Lists nested in rows
teams.hint: Each team's members are a list nested in the team's row. The server sends them inside the rows of initialData: they are in the HTML and are each list's baseline. Add or remove a member and that list is dirty; “Reset to the server's data” calls store.reset() and brings the server's members back. The block has a store of its own, so the reset reaches no other block.

flow.subtitle: Step flows (defineFlow) under SSR. The server renders each flow's active step but enters none: no onEnter, no resolver. The browser enters it once. A step with server data skips its request; a step without it arrives in the HTML as its loading state.
flow.lastStep: The last step of this flow.

onboarding.title: A flow whose first step has server data
onboarding.hint: The profile step's resolve got its result as initialData: the fields are in the HTML, and the server entered no step. The browser enters it once: onEnter, then onReady right away, and its resolver is not called. The team step has no server data: entering it runs its resolver once. Its result is cached, so Back and then Next again request nothing. onEnter counts every entry, onReady fires once per step.

booking.title: A flow whose first step has no server data
booking.hint: No initialData here. In server mode the active step's resolve is held: the step reads loading: true, so the HTML has its skeleton. The browser enters the step: onEnter, its resolver once, then onReady when the result lands.

slot.loading: Looking for a free review slot…

runtime.subtitle: When a store starts its resolvers, where it lives and how the provider's context reaches it: nothing starts during the server render, the browser starts each resolver once, every component instance gets a store of its own, and a nested provider's context is followed live.

lists.lazyRead: Lazy list, read by this block

serverMode.title: 1 · Server mode: nothing starts until store.start()
serverMode.hint: A server render has no window, so its store is in server mode and calls no resolver. This store passes server: true: usePalistor then leaves the start to the caller, and the store stays held in the browser as well. Both lists read loading: true (the lazy one because this block reads it, the eager one from the start), resolveStatus stays "idle" and nothing is called: the server's HTML and the hydrating render show the same. store.start() runs each held resolve once; a second call starts nothing.

client.title: 2 · In the browser usePalistor starts the store after the first commit
client.hint: The same lists with the default server option. The server sent the eager list as loading (the skeleton), and the browser's first render shows exactly that: usePalistor builds the store held and calls start() in an effect, once the component has committed. Then the eager list loads, although nothing has read its rows. A render React throws away therefore requests nothing. The lazy list waits for its first read, and reading its loading counts as one: this panel reads nothing until you press the button. A store made with new Palistor() is not held: in the browser its constructor starts it.
client.unread: Nothing has read this list yet: no request.

instances.title: 3 · One store per component instance
instances.hint: The page passes two teammates, and one card component renders each, calling usePalistor with its own teammate as initialData. Two instances, two stores: edit one card and the other stays as it was. The data is the store's baseline (Reset returns to it) and the answer of the card's resolver, which is never called. initialData exists only in the constructor: a store at module level lives as long as the server process and is shared by every request, so request data must never get into it.
instances.name: Name

context.title: 4 · The provider's context, live
context.hint: A nested PalistorProvider sets context.region for the store of this block. usePalistorContext() shows the merged context: workspace from the page's provider, region from this one. The mirror's resolve has contextDeps: ["region"], so without a region it waits: loading is false, no skeleton, no request. Picking a region starts it; another region re-runs it once, since the resolver read store.context.region. Picking the same region again hands the provider a new object with the same value: compared per key, that is no change, and nothing is sent.
context.waiting: No region yet: the resolve waits for its contextDeps.

products.subtitle: A list that holds all its rows sorts and filters them in the browser, without a request. A click on a column header sorts the products; the search and the filters narrow them on the client. The favorites are the same entities in a second list.

block.title: Products
block.hint: One list, loaded once by its resolver; it holds all its rows, so it sorts and filters them itself and the resolver is not called again. A column header steps through ascending, descending and the server's order (sort: true): numbers as numbers, text with "2" before "10" and case ignored, empty ratings last both ways, equal values in the server's order. The order is taken when you sort: a price edited in a row keeps its place and an added row stays at the bottom until the next header click or "Re-sort". The search, the category, the in-stock toggle and the price range are client fields of the list's filter block; they narrow the sorted rows and keep their order. One $all rule checks the price against both bounds (a reversed range is read the other way round); the price after "Shown" is a derived field. An edited price is written to the entity, which Favorites shows too.

filter.searchPlaceholder: Part of a title, for example: lamp

favorites.title: Favorites
favorites.hint: A second list over the same entities. Its resolver returns the saved favorites; ☆ in a product row adds one more with favorites.add(id), so the row is shared, not copied: a price edited here shows in the table and the other way round. ↑ and ↓ reorder through setItems. dirty compares the membership with the last loaded one; the rows' values take no part. "Restore saved" calls reload(): the saved membership and order come back, and so do the saved rows' values. store.reset() would not do this: it keeps the membership of a root list.
favorites.empty: No favorites. ☆ in a product row adds one.

orders.subtitle: A paginated list holds one page at a time, so the server sorts and filters it: a click on a column header, a search or a status change is one request for the first page.
orders.title: Orders
orders.hint: A HeroUI table over a paginated list. A click on a column header sorts on the server; the search and the status are server filter fields: the search sends its request {debounce} ms after the last keystroke, the status at once. Each change is one request for page 1, and the old rows stay, dimmed, until the new page lands.

tips.sort: Click a column header: the server sorts by it, one request for page 1. A second click reverses the order, a third one goes back to newest first; a sort seen a moment ago comes from the cache.
tips.prefetch: Hover over Next: the next page is fetched in advance (prefetch), so the click shows it at once.
tips.refresh: Refresh page fetches the page on screen again, and only that page: invalidate(page), one request.
tips.pageSize: Rows per page: setPageSize clears the cached pages and loads page 1 once.
tips.cache: The pages of the last three queries stay cached (maxCachedQueries): clear the search, pick the previous status or go back to the previous sort, and the rows come back without a request.
tips.stale: A cached page stays fresh for {seconds} s (staleTime). Open a page you saw longer ago: it shows at once, and is fetched again in the background.

customers.subtitle: The filter panel is a draft: the list and its requests change only when you press Apply. Each customer's invoices are a list nested in the row, with a pager of its own.

customers.title: Customers
customers.hint: A paginated server list, 8 rows a page, with a filter in "Apply" mode ($apply: "manual"). The panel's fields are a draft: choosing or typing there changes no row and sends no request; Apply (or Enter in the city field) sends one, from page 1, and Cancel brings the fields back. The quick search is the exception (apply: "auto"): one request once you stop typing, with the applied panel values, never the draft. The chips show what the list is filtered by; ✕ removes one with one request. The backend does not get the filter values as they are: the block's $toParams builds its query — the search trimmed and sent as q, an empty value left out. The line under the filters is the last request the backend received.
customers.pending: Waiting for you to stop typing…
customers.total: {count, plural, =0 {No customers} one {# customer} other {# customers}}

panel.title: Filters
panel.badge: {count, plural, one {# filter applied} other {# filters applied}}
panel.cityPlaceholder: Part of a city name; Enter applies

invoices.title: Customer invoices
invoices.hint: Each account owns its invoices: a list nested in the row, paginated per row. Every account has its own pager, its own page cache and its own requests: paging one account leaves the others where they are, and a page seen before comes from that account's cache without a request.
invoices.total: {count, plural, =0 {No invoices} one {# invoice} other {# invoices}}

feeds.subtitle: Two ways to page without page numbers: a feed that loads more at the bottom, and a journal that walks forward and back by cursor, under Suspense.

feed.title: Feed
feed.hint: An infinite list: Load more appends the next page with one request, nextCursor: null from the server ends the feed, and maxPages keeps at most {max} pages on screen. Newest / Oldest is a server sort: one request, and the window starts over at the first page. The window and the first visible post are saved in this browser: reload the page and both come back from storage, scrolled to where you were. The order is not saved: a window saved under Oldest is not reused, the reload starts at Newest.
feed.end: You've reached the end of the feed.
feed.shown: {count} posts on screen · {pages, plural, one {page {first}} other {pages {first}–{last}}}
feed.dropped: {count, plural, one {# older page} other {# older pages}} left the window (maxPages: {max})
feed.saved: The window and the reading position are saved in localStorage.

journal.title: Journal
journal.hint: Cursor mode: one page at a time. Forward fetches the next page; Back is always served from the cache, and so is Forward to a page already visited. The list has suspense: true, so its first load shows the Suspense fallback.
journal.cached: {count, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} in the cache
